title: Treasury Targets Cyber Scam Operators and Armed Group Facilitators in Southeast Asia
body: November 19, 2026 WASHINGTON —Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctioned three individuals involved in operating and facilitating cyber scam centers in Southeast Asia, as well as two affiliated companies.  The individuals designated today include operators of scam compounds that target Americans through virtual currency investment fraud and affiliates of armed groups that provide protection and support to scam-center networks in Southeast Asia. “Under President Trump’s leadership, Treasury has aggressively targeted overseas scam compounds to protect Americans from fraud,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent .  “We will continue to use all available tools to disrupt and dismantle the networks that enable scam compounds to operate.” These actions are being taken in furtherance of President Trump’s Executive Order (E.O.) 14390 of March 6, 2026, “Combating Cybercrime, Fraud, and Predatory Schemes Against American Citizens,” which orders the U.S. Government to unleash every available tool to stop foreign-backed criminal networks that exploit vulnerable Americans through cybercrime, cyber-enabled fraud, and extortion.  Today’s action further reflects OFAC’s coordination with the Federal Bureau of Investigation’s New York Field Office, Department of Justice’s Scam Center Strike Force, and the Drug Enforcement Administration, and the Homeland Security Task Force and National Coordination Center.  OFAC is taking today’s actions pursuant to E.O. 13694, as amended by E.O. 13757, E.O. 14144, and E.O. 14306 (“E.O. 13694, as further amended”). ZHAO HUI: A SCAM CENTER OPERATOR Zhao Hui (Zhao) is a Cambodian national who leased a scam center owned by the OFAC-designated Prince Group TCO and paid protection fees to the OFAC-designated leader of the Prince Group TCO, Chen Zhi .  In addition, Zhao owned a scam compound in Cambodia independent of Prince Group TCO.  At this scam compound, Zhao was directly involved in scam operations and managed this scam compound’s leases.  This scam compound primarily targeted Americans and Europeans.  Such scam compounds conduct virtual currency investment scams.  Since Zhao has leased a scam compound and owned and operated an additional scam compound in Cambodia, he has materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of virtual cryptocurrency investment scams, an activity described in subsection 1(a)(ii) of E.O. 13694, as further amended. Zhao is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, an activity described in subsection 1(a)(ii) of E.O. 13694, as further amended. Zhao is the chairman of the board of directors of Cambodia-based construction company Bei Fang Bo Lin Construction Decoration Co., Ltd . (Bei Fang Bo Lin) and management and consultancy company ZHZ Investment Consulting Co., Ltd. (ZHZ Investment). Bei Fang Bo Lin and ZHZ Investment are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended, for being owned or controlled by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Zhao Hui. THE DKBA’S FACILITATION OF SCAM COMPOUND ACTIVITY In recent years, armed groups in Burma have transformed a strip along the Thai-Burmese border into one of the world’s highest concentrations of scam centers.  The Democratic Karen Benevolent Army (DKBA) is an ethnic armed group previously designated by OFAC for supporting cyber scam centers in Burma that target Americans using fraudulent investment schemes.  DKBA actors not only provide security for scam compounds and permit their continued operation, but also actively participate in violence against victims of human trafficking trapped inside the compounds. Since December 2025, General Saw Shwe Wah has been the commander-in-chief of the DKBA, replacing General Saw Steel , who OFAC designated in November 2025 pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended. Colonel Saw A One is the DKBA commander who oversees security in the Three Pagodas Pass in Karen State near the Thai border.  The region has seen expansion of new buildings intended for telecom scam operations, with many scam actors entering the area with the assistance of the DKBA, which also protects them.  Saw A One reportedly owns a plantation where scam operations occur and has contracted for scam operations. Saw Shwe Wah and Saw A One are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended, for being or having been leaders, officials, senior executive officers, or members of the board of directors of the DKBA, a person whose property and interests in property are blocked pursuant to E.O. 13694, as further amended. SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S.  persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons. Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis.  OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities involving designated or otherwise blocked persons.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.  Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades U.S. sanctions.  Individuals located in the U.S. or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to FinCEN’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000. The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the SDN List, but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List, when consistent with relevant statutes and other authorities.   The ultimate goal of sanctions is to bring about a positive change in behavior.  What constitutes a sufficient change in circumstance will vary based on context, including the status of the broader geopolitical circumstances affecting the national security and foreign policy interests implicated by the declared national emergency. For more information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on How to Request Removal from an OFAC List . title: November 18, 2026 - FDA Approves First Drug to Treat Neurological Symptoms of Type 3 Gaucher Disease
body: FDA News Release FDA Approves First Drug to Treat Neurological Symptoms of Type 3 Gaucher Disease For Immediate Release: November 18, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved Infilbray (venglustat) tablets, the first treatment for the neurological symptoms of Type 3 Gaucher disease (GD3) in adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 15 kg (approximately 33 pounds). Infilbray crosses the blood-brain barrier to reduce the accumulation of harmful substances in the body and brain. “For patients with Type 3 Gaucher disease, harmful substances build up in the brain without a way to stop them, but this drug's ability to cross the blood-brain barrier means it can get to the source of the buildup driving the neurological symptoms,” said Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas, J.D. “This approval reflects the FDA’s commitment to advancing therapeutic options for patients with rare diseases and brings an important new treatment to patients and the healthcare providers who care for them.” GD3 is a rare, inherited condition in which the body cannot properly break down fatty substances, called glucosphingolipids, due to a deficient or malfunctioning enzyme. As these substances accumulate in organs, tissues, and the brain, patients experience a wide range of serious health problems over time. Unlike type 1 Gaucher disease, GD3 also affects the brain and nervous system, causing difficulties with balance, coordination, speech, memory, and thinking — symptoms that can worsen progressively and significantly impact quality of life. Infilbray works as a glucosylceramide synthase inhibitor, reducing the buildup of harmful substances throughout the body and, critically, within the brain. The FDA’s approval of Infilbray is supported by data from a randomized, double-blind, multicenter clinical study enrolling 43 patients aged 12 years and older with GD3 who had previously been treated with enzyme replacement therapy and had achieved systemic disease stabilization. Participants received either Infilbray orally once daily or intravenous enzyme replacement therapy every two weeks for 52 weeks. Treatment effectiveness was evaluated using two assessments that capture the neurological symptoms central to daily life in patients with GD3, including those related to ataxia (loss of muscle control and coordination) and cognitive function. At Week 52, patients treated with Infilbray demonstrated improvement on a measure that combined both assessments compared to those taking enzyme replacement therapy for the treatment of non-neurologic manifestations of GD3. The most frequently reported side effects of Infilbray include gastrointestinal symptoms as well as adverse effects on mood. Serious psychiatric risks, including suicidal ideation and behavior, have been reported. Potential risks identified from animal studies include potential clouding of vision in younger patients and adverse effects on fetal development when drug is taken during pregnancy. More information on side effects can be found in the drug labeling. Infilbray was granted Orphan Drug designation as well as Priority Review . The approval of Infilbray was granted to Genzyme Corporation, a Sanofi Company. Media: FDA Request for Comment 202-690-6343 Consumer: 888-INFO-FDA The FDA, an agency within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, protects the public health by assuring the safety, effectiveness, and security of human and veterinary drugs, vaccines and other biological products for human use, and medical devices. The agency also is responsible for the safety and security of our nation’s food supply, cosmetics, dietary supplements, radiation-emitting electronic products, and for regulating tobacco products. ###

title: Treasury’s Office of Cybersecurity and Critical Infrastructure Protection Issues Annual Consumer Advisory on Holiday Scams
body: November 18, 2026 WASHINGTON – Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Cybersecurity and Critical Infrastructure Protection (OCCIP) released its annual holiday advisory to help consumers protect themselves from the seasonal surge in cyber-enabled scams and online fraud. As frauds and scams continue to proliferate, including through the use of super intelligence, it is important to remember that anyone can be a victim of fraud. Learn how to identify fraudulent activity, disrupt scammers, and report incidents quickly to keep yourself and others safe. This holiday season, Treasury urges consumers to stay vigilant, be proactive, and respond quickly if they believe they are being targeted. Share your stories and experiences with your community to help teach others how to stay safe from scams. "As cybercriminals increasingly leverage super intelligence (SI) to carry out more sophisticated and convincing scams, it is more important than ever for Americans to remain vigilant this holiday season." said Cory Wilson, Deputy Assistant Secretary for Cybersecurity and Critical Infrastructure Protection.  "Cybercriminals are exploiting SI to impersonate trusted individuals, businesses, and even loved ones, putting Americans and their hard-earned money at risk.  Treasury remains committed to strengthening consumer resilience against cyber-enabled fraud through education, awareness, and actionable guidance. We encourage all Americans to take a moment to verify suspicious requests, recognize the warning signs of fraud, and report all suspected scams to the appropriate authorities." Access OCCIP’s Staying Cyber-Safe this Holiday Season . Report fraud to the Federal Trade Commission at ReportFraud.ftc.gov and the Federal Bureau of Investigation Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) . ###

title: Treasury International Capital Data for September
body: November 18, 2026 WASHINGTON – The U.S. Department of the Treasury today released Treasury International Capital (TIC) data for September 2026.  The next release, which will report on data for October 2026, is scheduled for December 15, 2026. The sum total in September of all net foreign acquisitions of long-term securities, short-term U.S. securities, and banking flows was a net TIC inflow of $261.0 billion.  Of this, net foreign private inflows were $267.0 billion, and net foreign official outflows were $6.0 billion. Foreign residents increased their holdings of long-term U.S. securities in September; their net purchases were $186.7 billion.  Net purchases by private foreign investors were $148.3 billion, and net purchases by foreign official institutions were $38.4 billion. U.S. residents increased their holdings of long-term foreign securities, with net purchases of $31.4 billion. After including adjustments, such as estimated foreign portfolio acquisitions of U.S. stocks through stock swaps, overall net foreign purchases of long-term securities are estimated to have been $155.3 billion in September. Foreign residents increased their holdings of U.S. Treasury bills by $3.5 billion.  Foreign resident holdings of all dollar-denominated short-term U.S. securities and other custody liabilities decreased by $2.9 billion. Banks’ own net dollar-denominated liabilities to foreign residents increased by $108.6 billion. Complete data are available on the Treasury website here . ### About TIC Data The monthly data on holdings of long-term securities, as well as the monthly table on Major Foreign Holders of Treasury Securities, reflect foreign holdings of U.S. securities collected primarily on the basis of custodial data.  These data help provide a window into foreign ownership of U.S. securities, but they cannot attribute holdings of U.S. securities with complete accuracy.  For example, if a U.S. Treasury security purchased by a foreign resident is held in a custodial account in a third country, the true ownership of the security will not be reflected in the data.  The custodial data will also not properly attribute U.S. Treasury securities managed by foreign private portfolio managers who invest on behalf of residents of other countries.  In addition, foreign countries may hold dollars and other U.S. assets that are not captured in the TIC data.  For these reasons, it is difficult to draw precise conclusions from TIC data about changes in the foreign holdings of U.S. financial assets by individual countries. title: Operation Economic Outcast Targets Iran’s Proxy Networks
body: November 18, 2026 Targets Include Hizballah-Affiliated Charity, Gold and Cash Smuggling Network WASHINGTON —Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) designated the Wa Ta’awanu Association (Wa Ta’awanu), a Hizballah-affiliated charity that provides cover for Hizballah’s activities under the guise of delivering humanitarian services. OFAC today also designated members of a Lebanon- and Türkiye-based gold and cash smuggling network run by Hizballah and Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps-Qods Force (IRGC-QF). “The Iranian regime’s attempts to infringe on Lebanon’s sovereignty through terror proxies like Hizballah will not be tolerated,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent .  “The U.S. government will continue to disrupt Iran’s attempts to exert influence in the region and fund its proxies.” Today’s action exposes Hizballah’s continued exploitation of civilian charitable organizations and its efforts to portray itself as a provider of humanitarian assistance.  It also increases pressure on the group’s illicit financing networks as Hizballah seeks to resist growing calls and international pressure to disarm. Today’s action is being taken pursuant to the United States’ counterterrorism authority, Executive Order (E.O.) 13224, as amended.  The U.S. Department of State designated Hizballah as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist pursuant to E.O. 13224 on October 31, 2001, for having committed, or posing a significant risk of committing, acts of terrorism that threaten the security of U.S. nationals or the national security, foreign policy, or economy of the United States.  Previously, the U.S. Department of State had designated Hizballah as a Foreign Terrorist Organization (FTO) pursuant to section 219 of the Immigration and Nationality Act on October 8, 1997.  OFAC also designated Hizballah pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, on August 20, 2026 for being owned, controlled, or directed by, or having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, the IRGC-QF. HIZBALLAH’S ABUSE OF THE CHARITABLE SECTOR Hizballah-affiliated Wa Ta’awanu is a Lebanon-based charity that provides emergency relief services for southern Lebanon while also channeling outside donor funds toward Hizballah’s terrorist activities.  In July 2026, as part of the June 26, 2026 Trilateral Framework between the United States, Lebanon, and Israel, the Lebanese Armed Forces moved into areas previously held by the Israeli military to secure those areas and ensure that they were free from Hizballah fighters and weapons.  However, Wa Ta’awanu provides a pretext for Hizballah’s militant activities in the pilot zones, preventing disarmament and inhibiting Lebanese government efforts to safeguard these areas.  Wa Ta’awanu founder Afif Abdel Rida Chouman leads the charity and coordinates the organization’s activities at Hizballah’s direction. Wa Ta’awanu and Afif Abdel Rida Chouman are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Hizballah. HIZBALLAH GOLD AND CASH NETWORK In coordination with Hizballah financial officials, Lebanese businessman and money changer Hassan Khechen and his brother Ibrahim Khechen have transferred significant funds over the course of their operations from the IRGC-QF to Lebanon on behalf of Hizballah.  Hassan Khechen is the owner of Lebanon-based Gold Global Company , which he uses to transfer money from several transit countries to Lebanon for Hizballah.  Hassan Khechen’s network also employs couriers to transfer funds in cash across borders.  Hassan Khechen’s brother, Ibrahim Khechen, also participates in Hizballah’s money smuggling network and has links to a related courier who was arrested in February 2025 at the Beirut airport with $2.5 million in his hand luggage.  Türkiye-based and Hizballah-affiliated Sankari Gold Kuyumculuk Ticaret Limited Sirketi (Sankari Gold), also controlled by Hassan Khechen, assists Gold Global Company in moving gold bullion and cash from Africa. Hassan Khechen and Ibrahim Khechen are being designated pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for having materially assisted, sponsored, or provided financial, material, or technological support for, or goods or services to or in support of, Hizballah.  Gold Global Company and Sankari Gold is being designated pursuant to E.O. 13224, as amended, for being owned, controlled, or directed by, or for having acted or purported to act for or on behalf of, directly or indirectly, Hassan Khechen. SANCTIONS IMPLICATIONS As a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.  In addition, any entities that are owned, directly or indirectly, individually or in the aggregate, 50 percent or more by one or more blocked persons are also blocked.  Unless authorized by a general or specific license issued by OFAC, or exempt, OFAC’s regulations generally prohibit all transactions by U.S. persons or within (or transiting) the United States that involve any property or interests in property of designated or otherwise blocked persons. Violations of U.S. sanctions may result in the imposition of civil or criminal penalties on U.S. and foreign persons.  OFAC may impose civil penalties for sanctions violations on a strict liability basis. OFAC’s Economic Sanctions Enforcement Guidelines provide more information regarding OFAC’s enforcement of U.S. economic sanctions.  In addition, financial institutions and other persons may risk exposure to sanctions for engaging in certain transactions or activities involving designated or otherwise blocked persons.  The prohibitions include the making of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services by, to, or for the benefit of any designated or blocked person, or the receipt of any contribution or provision of funds, goods, or services from any such person.  Non-U.S. persons are also prohibited from causing or conspiring to cause U.S. persons to wittingly or unwittingly violate U.S. sanctions, as well as engaging in conduct that evades U.S. sanctions.  Individuals located in the United States or abroad who provide information about sanctions violations to the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network’s whistleblower incentive program may be eligible for awards if the information they provide leads to a successful enforcement action that results in monetary penalties exceeding $1,000,000. Furthermore, engaging in certain transactions involving the persons designated today may risk the imposition of secondary sanctions on participating foreign financial institutions.  OFAC can prohibit or impose strict conditions on opening or maintaining, in the United States, a correspondent account or a payable-through account of a foreign financial institution that knowingly conducts or facilitates any significant transaction on behalf of a person who is designated pursuant to the relevant authority. The power and integrity of OFAC sanctions derive not only from OFAC’s ability to designate and add persons to the SDN List, but also from its willingness to remove persons from the SDN List, when consistent with relevant statutes and other authorities.   A goal of sanctions is to bring about a positive change in behavior.  What constitutes a sufficient change in circumstance will vary based on context, including the status of the broader geopolitical circumstances affecting the national security and foreign policy interests implicated by the declared national emergency.  OFAC sanctions determinations, including removal determinations, are made consistent with Administration foreign policy and national security policies and priorities.  For more information concerning the process for seeking removal from an OFAC list, including the SDN List, or to submit a request, please refer to OFAC’s guidance on How to Request Removal from an OFAC List. title: November 17, 2026 - FDA Launches the Global Reliance Disclosure Program to Expand Patient Access to Medicines Worldwide
body: FDA News Release FDA Launches the Global Reliance Disclosure Program to Expand Patient Access to Medicines Worldwide For Immediate Release: November 17, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today announced the Global Reliance Disclosure Program (GRDP), a landmark initiative that will fundamentally transform how the FDA's regulatory drug and biologic approval decisions are leveraged by health authorities around the world. The GRDP marks a major step forward in the FDA's global leadership and may accelerate patient access to innovative therapies throughout the world. The GRDP enables the FDA to more efficiently share minimally redacted approval packages, including the FDA's detailed scientific and regulatory assessments, directly with companies who can then share them with regulatory authorities outside of the United States, empowering those authorities to rely on the FDA's rigorous, science-based review decisions rather than conducting duplicative and time-consuming product evaluations of their own, while maintaining sovereignty over their regulatory decision. "The GRDP is a prime example of America First policies improving public health worldwide," said Grace Graham, FDA Deputy Commissioner for Policy, Legislation, and International Affairs . "The FDA is the global gold standard and making it easier for applicants to leverage our detailed scientific assessments to facilitate faster access for patients everywhere is an example of America’s continued interest in advancing global health under the Trump Administration." The GRDP launched on Oct. 30, with a President's Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) tentative approval for lenacapavir , a drug indicated for both HIV prevention and treatment. This is an especially meaningful starting point given PEPFAR's life-saving mission to combat HIV/AIDS in some of the world's most vulnerable populations. The GRDP is currently available to PEPFAR tentative approvals, excluding tentatively approved abbreviated new drug application products. However, the FDA intends to expand the GRDP in January 2027 to all novel drug and biologics (New Molecular Entity New Drug Applications and 351(a) Biologics License Applications), dramatically broadening the program's reach and impact. The FDA also intends to launch a pathway in early 2027 to expedite an applicant’s ability to request their minimally redacted action packages for approved and licensed drugs and biologics, accelerating global access to medicines that are already on the market in the United States and have been found to be safe and effective by the FDA. To receive a minimally redacted application approval package as part of the GRDP, applicants must request to participate within 10 calendar days of approval and confirm the application package is being submitted to a foreign regulatory authority in support of a marketing application. Applicants with eligible GRDP applications will receive detailed information in FDA approval letters and the agency intends to provide the minimally redacted package on an expedited basis. Requests for minimally redacted approval packages for other purposes will not be processed under the GRDP and should be submitted as a Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) request. “In an era of increasing global interdependence in pharmaceutical development and supply chains, the FDA's leadership is most effective when it is collaborative,” said Mark Abdoo, FDA Associate Commissioner for Global Policy and Strategy . “The GRDP reflects a forward-looking vision of regulatory leadership: one defined not by exclusivity, but by the willingness to share expertise, elevate global standards, and put patients first — wherever they are.” The GRDP addresses one of the most persistent and consequential challenges in global health: the gap between regulatory approval in high-capacity countries and patient access in lower-resource settings. When a drug is approved by the FDA, patients in many parts of the world may wait months or years longer for their own national health authority to complete an independent review due to limited regulatory capacity and resources. Beyond individual product approvals, the GRDP supports global health security. Harmonized regulatory decisions reduce the risk of fragmented or inconsistent product standards across markets, helping to ensure that the same high-quality therapies reach patients regardless of where they live, including here in the United States. title: November 17, 2026 - FDA Approves First Drug Shown to Help Patients with Infantile-Onset Niemann-Pick Disease Type C Live Longer
body: FDA News Release FDA Approves First Drug Shown to Help Patients with Infantile-Onset Niemann-Pick Disease Type C Live Longer New therapy offers a meaningful treatment option for families facing a rare and serious childhood disease For Immediate Release: November 17, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved Lembaz (adrabetadex) injection, the first treatment shown to help people with a severe form of Niemann-Pick disease type C (NPC) live longer. Lembaz is approved to reduce the risk of death in adult and pediatric patients who weigh at least 7 kg (about 15 pounds) and whose neurological symptoms began before age 6, also known as infantile-onset NPC. “For families living with Niemann-Pick disease type C, today’s approval marks an important milestone,” said Acting FDA Commissioner Kyle Diamantas, J.D. “For the first time, there is a treatment shown to help adults and children with this serious disease live longer, and we are committed to continuing to support the development of therapies for the rare disease community.” Niemann-Pick disease type C (NPC) is a rare, inherited lysosomal storage disorder affecting an estimated 1 in 150,000 people, in which the body cannot properly process cholesterol and other fats inside cells. Over time, these substances accumulate — particularly in the brain — causing progressive neurological decline, including loss of movement, coordination, and the ability to swallow. Patients whose neurological symptoms begin before age 6 face the most serious form of the disease. Prior to this approval action, two therapies were approved for NPC, but neither has been shown to reduce the risk of death. Both carry age and weight restrictions that limit access for the youngest and most seriously affected patients. Lembaz is the first FDA-approved therapy to reduce the risk of death in adults and children weighing at least 7 kg (about 15 pounds) with NPC whose neurological symptoms began before age 6. A trained healthcare provider gives Lembaz as an injection directly into the spinal canal — a procedure called an intrathecal injection — every two weeks. To assess whether Lembaz reduced the risk of death, the FDA examined the survival of 36 patients treated with Lembaz across three clinical studies and an expanded access program. All patients had neurological manifestations of NPC that occurred prior to age 6. Patients treated with Lembaz had longer overall survival compared to the matched external control group, with a 55% reduction in the risk of death. The median survival time was 8.5 years for the treated group compared with 4.9 years in the control group. This survival benefit was observed regardless of whether patients were also taking miglustat, a therapy used off-label in NPC. The most common side effects of Lembaz include problems with hearing, balance and coordination, fatigue, vomiting, back pain, headache, fever, diarrhea, nausea, and cough. Lembaz carries a boxed warning for hearing impairment, including permanent hearing loss. A comprehensive hearing evaluation should be performed on patients before starting Lembaz and regularly throughout treatment, and dose adjustments may be needed based on the results of these evaluations. Lembaz received Breakthrough Therapy designation. The FDA granted approval of Lembaz to Mandos, LLC, a subsidiary of Beren Therapeutics, PBC. title: FinCEN Issues Proposed Rule to Strengthen Customer Due Diligence Requirements for Covered Financial Institutions
body: November 17, 2026 WASHINGTON —Today, the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) issued a proposed rule to strengthen customer due diligence requirements, which are integral to efforts to combat money laundering and counter the financing of terrorism. FinCEN issues this proposal as a part of Treasury’s implementation of Executive Order 14406, Restoring Integrity to America’s Financial System . “Financial institutions are on the front lines of protecting our financial systems from criminal organizations and cartels that target law-abiding businesses and workers,” said Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent . “This proposed rule cuts unnecessary burden, gives institutions more flexibility to effectively combat risk, and strengthens our fight against financial crime.” The proposed rule would amend customer due diligence requirements to: explicitly provide that covered financial institutions can obtain additional information about beneficial owners of a legal entity customer that may be useful in mitigating risk or addressing supervisory concerns; codify exceptive relief FinCEN issued removing the requirement for covered financial institutions to identify and verify the beneficial owners of a legal entity customer each time the customer opens a new account; and specify information that a covered financial institution must obtain about each beneficial owner of a legal entity customer. FinCEN welcomes public comments. The comment period closes 60 days after the proposed rule’s publication in the Federal Register . Resources Notice of Proposed Rulemaking Fact Sheet ###

title: Treasury, IRS Issue Final Rules to Help Hardworking Americans Build a Financially Secure Retirement
body: November 17, 2026 SECURE 2.0 Final Regulations Expand Automatic Enrollment in Workplace Retirement Plans WASHINGTON — The U.S. Department of the Treasury and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) today issued final regulations to help more Americans save for retirement through their workplaces. The regulations implement a key provision of the SECURE 2.0 Act, providing employers with clear guidance on automatic enrollment for certain 401(k) and 403(b) retirement plans. The rules help workers build retirement savings while preserving their control over how much they contribute. Treasury estimates that SECURE 2.0’s automatic enrollment expansion provision will increase retirement savings by an average of $4.2 billion annually over the 2023-2032 period. “A financially secure retirement is a cornerstone of the American Dream, and every worker deserves the opportunity to achieve it,” said Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent . “Today’s rules help more American families and workers build retirement savings while keeping them in control of their contributions, and give employers the clarity and flexibility to invest in their employees’ futures.” “With the SECURE 2.0 regulations in place, American families will be able to boost their savings and keep more of their hard-earned money through their automatic enrollment in a retirement account,” said IRS Chief Executive Officer Frank J. Bisignano . “These regulations reduce the administrative burden placed on taxpayers when making long-term financial decisions. More broadly, they further the IRS goal of improving taxpayer service by making interactions with the Service simpler and easier.” STRENGTHENING AMERICANS’ RETIREMENT SAVINGS The final regulations implement a key provision of the SECURE 2.0 Act by clarifying requirements for plan sponsors and simplifying certain participant notices. Covered retirement plans generally must automatically enroll eligible employees at a contribution rate of three percent. After an initial participation period, the default contribution rate must generally increase by at least one percentage point each year until it reaches at least ten percent, subject to a fifteen percent maximum. Employees may opt out or choose a different contribution rate. The final regulations generally apply to retirement plan years beginning after December 31, 2027, giving employers time to make necessary administrative changes. The final regulations: Clarify statutory exceptions for qualifying small and new businesses, governmental plans, church plans, and SIMPLE 401(k) plans; Give employers flexibility in the timing and amount of automatic contribution increases, within statutory limits; Simplify plan communications by allowing certain required notices to be combined and reducing annual notice requirements for qualifying employees who are not participating, provided they receive annual reminders and any plan documents they are entitled to request; and Explain how automatic enrollment requirements apply following plan mergers. The final regulations are available here . ###

title: November 9, 2026 - FDA Approves First Factor Xla Inhibitor to Help Prevent Stroke in Certain Adults at High Risk
body: FDA News Release FDA Approves First Factor Xla Inhibitor to Help Prevent Stroke in Certain Adults at High Risk For Immediate Release: November 09, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today approved Sunharbo (asundexian) 50 mg tablets, the first factor XIa (FXIa) inhibitor for use in combination with antiplatelet therapy to reduce the risk of stroke in adults following a recent mild-to-moderate non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke (a stroke caused by a clot that did not originate in the heart) or a high-risk transient ischemic attack (TIA), often called a “mini-stroke.” “Stroke is a leading cause of disability and death in the United States, and survivors are at risk of having another stroke,” said Hylton V. Joffe, M.D., MMSc, Director of the Office of Cardiology, Hematology, Endocrinology, and Nephrology in the FDA’s Center for Drug Evaluation and Research . “Today’s approval represents a meaningful advance for patients and health care providers seeking a new option for secondary stroke prevention.” The effectiveness of Sunharbo was demonstrated in the OCEANIC-STROKE study , a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 study that enrolled 12,327 adults. Participants had a recent non-cardioembolic ischemic stroke (NIH Stroke Scale ≤15) or high-risk TIA and were randomly assigned to Sunharbo or placebo within 72 hours of symptom onset. Both groups also received antiplatelet therapy. Sunharbo 50 mg once daily significantly reduced the risk of ischemic stroke by 26% compared to placebo over a median treatment of 14.2 months. The overall rate of major bleeding was similar between the Sunharbo and placebo groups but was increased with Sunharbo in patients older than 75 years and during the first 90 days of treatment. Gastrointestinal bleeding occurred more commonly with Sunharbo compared to placebo. The most frequently reported adverse reaction (occurring in 3% or greater of Sunharbo-treated patients) was diarrhea. Concomitant use with medicines that are combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inducers (such as carbamazepine) is not recommended because these medicines may decrease Sunharbo’s effectiveness. Sunharbo is not recommended in patients with moderate or severe hepatic impairment. Sunharbo should be withheld at least 24 hours before elective surgery or invasive procedures and for at least 24 hours after thrombolysis for acute ischemic stroke. Sunharbo is not approved for stroke prevention in patients with atrial fibrillation. The FDA granted Sunharbo Fast Track and Priority Review designations. The approval was granted to Bayer HealthCare Pharmaceuticals Inc., Whippany, N.J. title: November 5, 2026 - FDA Grants Accelerated Approval to a New Treatment for Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma
body: FDA News Release FDA Grants Accelerated Approval to a New Treatment for Head and Neck Squamous Cell Carcinoma For Immediate Release: November 05, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today granted accelerated approval to Rybrevant Faspro (amivantamab and hyaluronidase-lpuj) for the treatment of adults with recurrent or metastatic head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) whose disease has progressed on or after platinum-based chemotherapy and immunotherapy. HNSCC is an aggressive, life-threatening disease for which there is a high unmet need for effective therapies. Rybrevant Faspro is not indicated as a treatment for patients with oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma that is associated with human papillomavirus (HPV). Approval was based on trial results showing that more than double the percentage of patients responded to the drug compared to currently approved therapies. This is the first approval in 10 years of a drug for patients with recurrent or metastatic HNSCC who had received prior platinum-based chemotherapy. “Today’s approval represents a meaningful step forward for patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, a disease where treatment options have historically been limited and outcomes remain poor,” said Angelo De Claro, M.D., director of the FDA’s Oncology Center of Excellence . “This therapy offers patients and their physicians a new option with the potential to make a real difference in people’s lives.” The Accelerated Approval Program allows for earlier approval of drugs that treat serious conditions and fill an unmet medical need based on surrogate or intermediate endpoints. In this case, accelerated approval of Rybrevant Faspro was granted based on overall response rate and duration of response. Since it is not yet confirmed whether this will translate into a clinically meaningful benefit in long-term outcomes, the FDA has required confirmatory studies to verify and describe clinical benefit. In an open-label, multicenter clinical trial involving 102 patients with recurrent or metastatic HNSCC, Rybrevant Faspro had an overall response rate of 42%, meaning these patients saw their tumor either decrease in size or disappear. Of those patients who had a response, 56% had a response lasting six months or longer. Currently approved therapies are associated with an overall response rate of around 20% or less and poor outcomes. The prescribing information for use as a single agent includes warnings and precautions for hypersensitivity and administration-related reactions, interstitial lung disease (ILD)/pneumonitis, dermatologic adverse reactions, ocular toxicity, and harm to an unborn baby. The FDA granted Rybrevant Faspro Breakthrough Therapy designation for this indication. The approval was granted to Janssen Biotech, Inc. November 2, 2026 - FDA Provides Clarity to Support Cell and Gene Therapy Development and Quality
body: FDA News Release FDA Provides Clarity to Support Cell and Gene Therapy Development and Quality FDA issues final guidance for cell and gene therapy manufacturers, recommends building potency assurance into every stage of a therapy’s lifecycle — from early development through patient delivery For Immediate Release: November 02, 2026 The U.S. Food and Drug Administration today issued final guidance for manufacturers of cellular and gene therapy (CGT) products to implement a comprehensive, science- and risk-based plan for making sure their products meet potency standards. The guidance provides FDA’s recommendations for a Potency Assurance Strategy, which guides manufacturers to test and verify — before a product reaches a patient — that every batch meets a defined standard of potency to do what the product is supposed to do therapeutically. The Potency Assurance for Cellular and Gene Therapy Products final guidance replaces FDA's 2011 potency testing guidance for CGT products and applies to treatments for serious and often life-threatening conditions. By law, manufacturers are expected to verify that their products work as intended, from the time of approval through post-approval monitoring. This final guidance provides FDA’s current thinking and recommendations on how manufacturers can meet that requirement. "Patients who receive cellular and gene therapies are often battling serious or life-threatening conditions, such as cancers and rare diseases, and they deserve the assurance that the product administered to them will perform as intended," said Karim Mikhail, B. Pharm., M.S., Director of the Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research . "This guidance reflects the FDA's commitment to ensuring America remains the best place in the world to innovate — and that innovation is matched by the highest standards of product quality and patient safety." The guidance provides flexible, risk-based recommendations for manufacturers on how to integrate potency considerations at every stage of development and commercialization — from early-phase investigational new drug (IND) submissions through biologics license application (BLA) approval and continued post-market verification. Key topics include controls for variability in raw materials, testing during manufacturing, and lab tests that confirm each batch is biologically active in a way that matches its intended therapeutic effect. The guidance also addresses specialized considerations for products with short shelf lives, viral vector gene therapies, and patient-specific therapies. By giving manufacturers a clear, predictable roadmap, this guidance supports faster access to safe and effective therapies for patients who often have no other treatment options — many of whom receive products made individually for a single person. In doing so, it advances the FDA's public health pillars: protecting patients through rigorous quality standards, promoting innovation by providing regulatory clarity, and reinforcing the integrity of the supply chain for some of the most complex medical products in existence. The FDA will host a webinar on December 10, 2026, to help stakeholders understand and implement the guidance.
